Undergraduate thesis · 2024–2025 · Defended in February 2025

Triple Roman Domination

Research into correctness and graph optimization: identified a counterexample, corrected an ILP formulation, and implemented GA and ACO for experimental evaluation.

Understand the resultsSee model and experiments

Scientific contribution

A counterexample before an optimization claim.

Contribution
Identified an invalid solution accepted by a published ILP formulation; implemented a corrected, reduced formulation.
Method
Formal constraint analysis, a counterexample, Python/Pyomo modeling, and GA and ACO implementations in C++.
Evidence
Counterexample and formulation → Experiments on 362 graphs →
Limitation
One run per instance; time-limited solvers may return a feasible solution without proving optimality. No general superiority claim for either metaheuristic.

The challenge

Save resources while maintaining protection.

Each region receives 0, 2, 3, or 4 legions; the goal is the cheapest protected graph.

I compared a genetic algorithm (FLGA), ant colony optimization with local search (ACO-FL), and an integer linear programming (ILP) reference.

How to read the results

Lower cost is better. Feasibility comes first.

Correctness before speed

A counterexample showed the published formulation accepted insufficient defense; I corrected its constraints.

ACO-FL wins on some graphs

On g75-.2, ACO-FL costs 34 versus FLGA’s 39, but remains above the proven optimum of 28.

FLGA also has an advantage

On g225-.8, FLGA reaches the optimum at 8; ACO-FL costs 12. The best strategy depends on graph structure.

Results cover 362 graphs; one run per instance is descriptive, not statistical proof.

My role and evidence

Reproducible implementation and evaluation.

I implemented the metaheuristics in C++ and the ILP model in Python, evaluated 362 graphs, and used irace for tuning. The repository has code, instances, and outputs.

The thesis was defended in 02/2025 and the degree completed on 19/08/2026. A gap without optimality proof compares found solutions, not distance to optimum.
